parsed.explanation: The operative regime layers a national binary-sex document and facility system onto a state that has expanded birth-sex restroom rules into higher education and operates freeze-frame prison treatment. The sharpest traveler exposure is at the border: a passport marker or appearance discrepancy can trigger secondary screening, refusal, and a possible fraud-based lifetime ban; existing X passports remain valid but new ones are not. Facilities exclusion is state-imposed in covered schools/colleges and national in government-funded single-sex facilities. Custody carries documented severe harm. National hate-crime law and litigation provide partial recourse but not a working remedy at the border or in facilities. No visitor-targeted violence pattern is documented, so this is not the catastrophic tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport/visa policy; X marker halted for new issues; discrepancy or reasonable doubt can lead refusal and possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation ongoing; fraud finding requires four elements and is not automatic; limited waiver.
entry_documents.interaction: Every visitor crosses the border; foreign passport marker or appearance mismatch can trigger secondary screening and case-note tagging.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; corrections policies remove hormones and impose conversion-style treatment; state freeze-frame prison treatment policy.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; courts have enjoined some national orders; no state placement or housing ruling is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border fraud suspicion or a facility/restroom arrest can move a traveler into custody, where state treatment rules then apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law requires public school and college students to use restrooms by sex assigned at birth; national order bars congruent use in government-funded single-sex facilities; several states criminalize some restroom use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: One plaintiff has a litigation injunction; local employment protections exist but do not cover facilities; no visitor-facing facility protection is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a covered public campus or federal building can be excluded or reported; enforcement against non-students is uncertain.

care_services.exposure: National hostility to gender-affirming care, proposed insurance bar for under-18s, custody hormone removal; 27 states ban minor care, though this state is not specified.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitor care; general emergency care is not addressed.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor or adult needing medication or care may face refusal, record flags, or custody confiscation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Justice Department reward memo references 'radical gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; national rhetoric is hostile.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo does not make gender ideology a reward criterion; national hate-crime law covers gender identity; some orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises official suspicion and reporting risk, especially if documents or activism draw attention.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order targets school gender-ideology support and teacher use of preferred names; minor care restrictions; state bathroom law covers students.
minors_guardians.protection: Court injunctions block some orders; no documented visitor-specific minor protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces heightened scrutiny if school or care settings or documents reveal transition.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific visitor violence is documented in the dossier; the state lacks a hate-crime statute and its sodomy law is unrepealed; national climate is hostile.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no state bias-crime law; local police response is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If assaulted, recourse may depend on national rather than state authorities; no pattern of police targeting is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation is unresolved; enforcement is uneven; a possible lifetime fraud finding and state facility exclusion lack a clear visitor remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties lawsuits, injunctions, national hate-crime statute, passport FAQ, and local employment protections exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may operate after harm or for specific plaintiffs, not as universal protection at the border or in facilities.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is document-mismatch denial with invasive review but no facility ban, no custody conversion policy, and no possible lifetime fraud ban. This jurisdiction is somewhat lower: the national border regime plus state facility exclusion and documented custody harm add severity.

0.55-B shows a functioning transit guideline and supervisor release. Here protections are litigation-dependent and do not reach the border or facility exposures, so this jurisdiction is materially lower.

0.75-C has a functioning patient-privacy directive and immediate care. Here no visitor care protection is documented, minor-care policy is hostile, and custody rules remove hormones, so this jurisdiction is much lower.

The sharpest traveler exposure is at the border: a passport marker or appearance discrepancy can trigger secondary screening, refusal, and a possible fraud-based lifetime ban; existing X passports are valid but new ones are not. Facilities exclusion is state-imposed in covered schools and colleges and national in government-funded single-sex facilities. Custody carries documented severe harm. National hate-crime law and litigation provide partial recourse but not a working remedy at the border or in facilities. No visitor-targeted violence pattern is documented, so this is not the catastrophic tier.
